answer: Fufu and egusi is a popular West African food pairing: fufu is a soft, starchy accompaniment, while egusi soup is a savoury dish thickened with ground melon-family seeds. In Nigerian cooking, the soup may include greens, peppers, fish or meat. Different communities prepare both components in distinct ways, so no single recipe represents every household.

facts.fact: The Pan-Atlantic University feature identifies ground egusi seeds as the main ingredient of the soup.
The Pan-Atlantic University feature records egusi soup served with eba, pounded yam and amala as well as other swallows.
Ozoz Sokoh's Nigerian Food 101 guide was published by Serious Eats on 31 March 2023.
A peer-reviewed review lists fufu, eba and amala among Nigerian swallow meals eaten with soups.
A research article on an egusi-okra meal describes egusi seeds as dried, shelled and ground for cooking.
Allrecipes' egusi soup recipe was last updated on 22 September 2026.
